title: Protocol for RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization in mouse meningeal whole mounts
protocol: Euthanize mice.
Transcardially perfuse euthanized mice with 10 mL sterile pharmaceutical grade saline containing heparin (100 U/mL).
Transcardially perfuse mice with 6 mL 10% neutral buffered formalin.
Cut away fur and skin covering the skull.
Make a transverse cut between the eye sockets using fine scissors.
Carefully cut posteriorly along the sides of the skull, starting at the transverse cut.
Use a pair of forceps to lift off the calvaria with meninges attached.
Fix the calvaria with associated meninges in 10% neutral buffered formalin overnight at room temperature in a 15 mL conical tube.
Separate the meninges from the brain using spring scissors if necessary while removing the skull cap.
Prepare a 24 well plate with two wells containing 1 mL of PBS for each meninges.
Briefly rinse a calvaria in PBS and place it under a stereomicroscope (optional but recommended).
Make sure meninges do not dry out by adding approximately 100 μL PBS.
Extract meningeal layers from the skull cap using fine forceps.
Loosen the meninges around the perimeter carefully.
Start peeling off meninges at the olfactory bulb area gently.
Continue loosening any attached areas with forceps.
Peel meninges towards the midline of the calvaria.
Pull meninges loose starting at the cerebellum and ending at the olfactory bulbs.
Place extracted meninges in the first well containing PBS.
Wash meningeal layers for 5 minutes on a shaker (70 rpm).
Transfer meninges to the second well with PBS using forceps.
Wash meningeal layers for another 5 minutes on a shaker (70 rpm).
Keep meninges in PBS for up to 1 hour at room temperature if mounting several samples sequentially.
Split calvaria down the midline using a razor blade before extracting meninges, generating two samples from each skull cap.
Mount extracted meningeal layers onto microscope slides by placing approximately 100 μL of PBS in the middle of the slide and adding washed meninges to the droplet.
Using fine forceps, gently spread meningeal tissue.
Remove liquid using a pipette and further spread the meninges.
Carefully remove remaining liquid with a paper tissue.
Dry the meninges on a flat surface overnight at room temperature.
Wash dried meninges by dipping them about 10 times in distilled water.
Dry meninges for 24 hours at 42°C or for at least three days at room temperature.
Set up equipment for target retrieval: Add 1 L distilled water to the water chamber of a Hamilton Beach vegetable steamer.
Put one container with 200 mL distilled water in the steaming compartment.
Put one container with 200 mL 1× target retrieval solution in the steaming compartment.
Start the preset steaming program, setting the duration for at least 1 h.
Use a thermometer to monitor the temperature of the target retrieval solution.
Lay slide with dried meninges flat on the bench.
When the target retrieval solution in the steamer reaches 90°C, add 4–5 drops of hydrogen peroxide to meninges and incubate for 10 min at RT.
Briefly wash meninges by placing slides in a Tissue Tek slide holder and dipping them in a Tissue Tek staining dish filled with distilled water.
Repeat wash.
Carefully open the steamer and submerge slides in the water for 15 s.
Transfer slides to the target retrieval solution and incubate for 10–15 min.
Carefully remove slides from the steamer and rinse them in a Tissue Tek staining dish filled with distilled water for 15 s.
Incubate slides in a Tissue Tek staining dish filled with 100% ethanol for 3 min at RT.
Heat 700 mL 1× target retrieval solution in a 1 L beaker on a hot plate until it reaches a mild boil.
Slowly submerge a slide rack with slides into the boiling target retrieval solution and continue to boil for 10–15 minutes.
Remove slides from the solution, rinse them briefly in distilled water.
Incubate slides in 100% ethanol for 3 minutes.
Proceed to step 8.
Remove slides from ethanol.
Dry slides at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Draw a border around the tissue on the slide using a hydrophobic barrier pen.
Dry the slides completely at room temperature, at least 10 minutes.
Transfer slides to the HybEz II hybridization system slide holder.
Add 4–5 drops of Protease Plus to each slide.
Incubate slides for 15–30 minutes at 40°C in a hybridization oven.
Rinse slides in distilled water.
Repeat rinse with fresh distilled water.
Remove excess liquid from slides by holding the slide holder vertically.
Dab the lower portion of each hydrophobic area carefully with a piece of tissue.
Add 100–150 μL probe mixture to each sample to cover tissue completely.
Incubate samples in a hybridization oven for 2 hours.
Wash slides in 200 mL of 1× wash buffer for 2 minutes with gentle agitation.
Repeat the washing step.
Remove excess liquid from slides and add 4–6 drops of AMP1.
Incubate slides in a hybridization oven for 30 minutes.
Wash slides with 1× wash buffer.
Remove excess liquid and add 4–6 drops of AMP2.
Incubate slides in a hybridization oven for 30 minutes.
Wash slides with 1× wash buffer.
Remove excess liquid from slides and add 4–6 drops of AMP3.
Incubate slides in a hybridization oven for 15 minutes.
Wash slides with 1× wash buffer.
Remove excess liquid from slides and add 4–6 drops of the correct HRP (e.g., HRP-C1).
Incubate slides in a hybridization oven for 15 minutes.
Wash slides with 1× wash buffer.
Remove excess liquid and add 100–150 μL of appropriate Opal dye as substrate for HRP.
Incubate slides in a hybridization oven for 30 minutes.
Wash slides with 1× wash buffer.
Remove excess liquid.
Add 4–6 drops HRP blocker to each slide.
Incubate in the hybridization oven for 15 min.
Wash slides with 1× wash buffer.
If using more than one probe, repeat step with other HRPs and opal dyes.
Reconstitute opal dyes following manufacturers’ directions.
Dilute reconstituted opal dyes at a ratio of 1:1500 in TSA buffer.
Protect sample from light after adding opal dyes.
If meninges detach from the microscope slide during staining, refer to troubleshooting problem 3.
Optional: Perform immunohistochemistry at this point, starting with step 14 below.
Remove excess liquid and add a few drops of DAPI to the slide.
Incubate for 30 s at RT.
Tap off excess DAPI.
Mount slides using a coverslip and mounting medium, e.g., ProLong Glass Antifade Mountant.
Let slides cure, protected from light, O/N at RT before viewing.
Wash slides two times with TBST wash buffer for two minutes each following the last HRP-blocker step and washes.
Add 100–150 μL of 10% normal serum diluted in TBSB to slides.
Incubate at RT for 30 min, protected from light, in a humidity chamber.
Tap slides to remove excess blocking solution.
Add 100–150 μL primary antibody diluted in TBSB within the hydrophobic barrier.
Incubate for 2 h at RT, protected from light, in a humidified chamber.
Wash slides in TBST with gentle agitation three times for 5 min each.
Add 100–150 μL HRP-conjugated secondary antibody diluted in TBSB to slides.
Incubate for 30 min at RT.
Wash slides in TBST with gentle agitation three times for 5 min each.
Add 100–150 μL of the appropriate Opal dye diluted in TSA buffer to each sample.
Incubate for 10 min at RT.
Wash slides in TBST with gentle agitation three times for 2 min each.
Counterstain and mount slides as described in step 13 above.
Image slides in a fluorescence microscope to visualize mRNA and protein expression.
Use a fluorescence microscope equipped with an appropriate light source and filter sets.
Analyze acquired images using an image analysis program, e.g., Fiji (ImageJ).
